meta.title: Schmitt trigger (comparator with hysteresis)
meta.tools: eelab mini-SPICE transient, noisy slow ramp input
meta.summary: Feed a slow, noisy ramp into a plain comparator and a Schmitt trigger: predict the hysteresis thresholds and count false transitions in each.
meta.problem: A slowly changing noisy signal makes a comparator chatter as it crosses the threshold. How much hysteresis stops it, and where exactly do the thresholds land?
meta.theory:
Inverting Schmitt trigger: input to (−), positive feedback R₁ (to ground) / R₂ (to output) on (+).
With output saturation $\pm V_{sat}$:
$$V_{T\pm}=\pm V_{sat}\frac{R_1}{R_1+R_2}$$
R₁ = 1 kΩ, R₂ = 47 kΩ, V_sat = 12 V → ±250 mV (500 mV window). Noise of amplitude below half the
window cannot cause a second transition.
